result_text:
A folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as mock resources, whatever the rest of the name is. That covers plain `mock/`, `mock.data/`, `mock(old)/` and `mock-größe/`. I didn't add tests for the new cases, and I didn't try any of these paths directly. The existing scoping tests in `codeanalyzer` pass.

In `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java` (lines 393–394), I changed two patterns:
- `.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` is now `.*/__mock[^/]*/.*`.
- `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` is now `.*/mock[^/]*/.*`.

The rest of the folder name can't contain a slash, so the match stays inside that one folder name:
- `remock/`, `demo/` and `src/main/java/` don't match, because the pattern needs a `/` immediately before `mock`.
- Files named `mock.java` or `mockery.java` don't match, because the pattern needs a `/` after the folder name.
- Windows-style paths work because the path matcher already converts backslashes to forward slashes.
- Every folder that was test code before (`mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/`, `mockStore/`) still matches.
